current_activity: Begins to arrive in Belgium from Italy in the last days of February (Operation Goldflake)
notes: Event date: the last days of February 1945 (Stacey, p. 529); 28 February is used as the date of the claim. Event definition: The division begins to arrive in Belgium from Italy in the last days of February in Operation Goldflake, the withdrawal of the 1st Canadian Corps from Italy and its reunion with the Canadian field force in north-west Europe; the 1st Canadian Armoured Brigade is in Belgium by mid-March. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 529: "The 5th Canadian Armoured Division began to arrive in Belgium in the last days of February". Location: Antwerp, Belgium (existing place PL0574) with a precision of 50 km. Location approximate: the point is Antwerp, a representative point in Belgium; the arrival places are not named and the day is not given. Location support: Stacey says Belgium and names no place (p. 529). Commander: Maj.-Gen. B. M. Hoffmeister (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 667: 5th Canadian Armoured Division, 20 Mar. 44 to 6 Jun. 45). Context: Only the time in the Western Front theatre is recorded; the division positions in Italy before this are deliberately not written (Canadian Batch 2 scope).

current_activity: Takes over the western sector of the island from the 49th Division, on the Waal and Neder Rijn
notes: Event date: 31 March 1945 (Stacey, p. 567). Event definition: The division takes over the western sector of the island between the Waal and the Neder Rijn from the 49th Division on the 31st, with the 11th Infantry Brigade and the Westminster Regiment reverting under it; its responsibilities extend downstream along the Waal to near Heerewaarden; the inter-divisional boundary runs from De Hulk, six miles west of the Nijmegen bridge, towards Arnhem. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 567: "reverted under Major-General B. M. Hoffmeister's 5th Canadian Armoured Division on the 31st, when that division took over the western sector of the island from the 49th"; "Hoffmeister's responsibilities extended downstream, along the line of the Waal, to near Heerewaarden". Location: Nijmegen area, Gelderland (existing place PL0554) with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: the point is Nijmegen, standing for the island sector that lies to its west; it is not a headquarters position. Location support: Stacey describes the island west of Nijmegen between the Waal and the Neder Rijn (p. 567). Commander: Maj.-Gen. B. M. Hoffmeister (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 667: 5th Canadian Armoured Division, 20 Mar. 44 to 6 Jun. 45). Context: Only the time in the Western Front theatre is recorded; the division positions in Italy before this are deliberately not written (Canadian Batch 2 scope).

current_activity: Operation Cleanser: Hoffmeister issues his orders for the thrust to the Ijsselmeer from his headquarters at Didam
notes: Event date: 14 April 1945 (Stacey, p. 576). Event definition: General Foulkes gives instructions to General Hoffmeister for the quick thrust north to the Ijsselmeer, and Hoffmeister issues his orders on 14 April from his temporary headquarters at Didam, planning to advance from Arnhem through Otterloo and Barneveld to Nijkerk; Stacey gives the afternoon for the instructions and noon for the orders on the same page. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 576: "the 5th Armoured Division was preparing the quick thrust north to the Ijsselmeer, for which General Foulkes gave instructions to General Hoffmeister on the afternoon of 14 April"; "As General Hoffmeister looked north-west from his temporary headquarters at Didam"; "At noon on the 14th Hoffmeister issued his orders". Location: Didam, Gelderland with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Stacey names Didam as the temporary headquarters of the division (p. 576). Commander: Maj.-Gen. B. M. Hoffmeister (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 667: 5th Canadian Armoured Division, 20 Mar. 44 to 6 Jun. 45). Context: Only the time in the Western Front theatre is recorded; the division positions in Italy before this are deliberately not written (Canadian Batch 2 scope).

current_activity: Cleanser: the 1st Division 3rd Brigade makes contact with the 5th Division at Barneveld on the 17th
notes: Event date: 17 April 1945 (Stacey, p. 579). Event definition: While the armour of the division fights towards the Ijsselmeer, the 3rd Brigade of the 1st Division, moving west from Apeldoorn, makes contact with the division at Barneveld on the 17th. current_activity: Hands its sector to the 1st Division on 19 April; passes under II Canadian Corps on 21 April to relieve the 3rd Division
notes: Event date: 21 April 1945 (Stacey, p. 591). Event definition: The division hands its sector to the 1st Division on 19 April, begins moving from western Holland on 21 April to assume its new responsibilities and passes under the 2nd Canadian Corps on the same date, with operational control of Friesland, Groningen, Drenthe and the northern part of Overijssel, and virtually completes its relief of the 3rd Division on 24 April. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 580: "the 5th Division handed its sector over to the 1st Division on 19 April"; p. 591: "On 21 April, as already mentioned, the division began moving from western Holland to assume its new responsibilities; it passed under the 2nd Canadian Corps on the same date"; p. 592: "The 5th Division virtually completed its relief of the 3rd Division on 24 April". Location: Groningen, Groningen (area of the new responsibilities) with a precision of 50 km. Location approximate: the point is the city of Groningen, standing for the large area given to the division; it is not a headquarters position. Location support: Stacey names the provinces of Friesland, Groningen, Drenthe and the northern portion of Overijssel (p. 591) and the area north and east of Groningen (p. 592). Commander: Maj.-Gen. current_activity: Delfzijl is completely cleared on 1 May by the 11th Brigade; the pocket at Weiwerd and Farmsum ends on the 2nd
notes: Event date: 1 May 1945 (Stacey, pp. 593-594). Event definition: The decisive assault on Delfzijl by The Cape Breton Highlanders of the 11th Brigade begins at 22:00 on 30 April and the port is completely cleared on 1 May; on 2 May the Irish Regiment of Canada ends resistance in the pocket at Weiwerd and Farmsum, taking 38 officers, including the garrison commander, and over 1300 other ranks. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 594: "Delfzijl was completely cleared on the 1st"; p. 593: "Not until the port fell (1 May) did the enemy evacuate this position by sea"; p. 594: "the Irish extinguished the remaining embers of resistance in the pocket at Weiwerd and Farmsum". Location: Delfzijl, Groningen with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Stacey names Delfzijl (pp. 593-594). Commander: Maj.-Gen. B. M. Hoffmeister (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 667: 5th Canadian Armoured Division, 20 Mar. 44 to 6 Jun. 45). Context: Only the time in the Western Front theatre is recorded; the division positions in Italy before this are deliberately not written (Canadian Batch 2 scope).
